title: The 20-second browser
question: Why does jelly see sometimes take 20 s and come back without a snapshot?
status: Open. jelly ask no longer waits for the browser to exit; jelly see still does (issue #6).

marks.label: First see: 20 s, no snapshot
marks.detail: The very first jelly see against a new daemon. The profile folder /tmp/jelly-chrome did not exist before this run.

show.after:
$ time jelly see plan
trial:plan · trial · v4 · made by agent · last change just now by agent
waits    a1 ask "Which order?" [a★/b] at #list
waits    a2 ask "Dead anchor?" [y/n] at #nope
!        No snapshot: the browser took longer than 20 s

real    0m20.006s

marks.label: render() waits for Chrome to exit
marks.detail: What the daemon does: one shared profile folder, a virtual time budget of 2.5 s, and it waits up to 20 s for the browser process to end. It does not look at whether the snapshot already arrived.

show.caption: src/server.rs, as it was

marks.label: By hand, with the time budget: 1 s
marks.detail: The same Chrome and the same page, run from a shell with its own profile folder. It dumped the page and exited.

show.after:
$ google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --virtual-time-budget=2500 \
    --dump-dom --user-data-dir=…/prof "http://127.0.0.1:7879/j/trial:plan/?agent=1" | wc -c
4588
exit 0   1s

marks.label: By hand, without it: never exits
marks.detail: Without --virtual-time-budget Chrome was still running when timeout killed it at 25 s. Left alone, this page does not let Chrome finish.

show.after:
$ timeout 25 google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --timeout=5000 \
    --dump-dom --user-data-dir=…/prof "http://127.0.0.1:7879/j/trial:plan/?agent=1" | wc -c
Terminated
exit 124   25s

marks.label: Snapshot arrives, screenshot times out
marks.detail: One command, two renders. The first posted its snapshot (the page text came back); the second, for the png, hit 20 s. So a render can do its work and still be counted as failed.

marks.label: Playwright's Chromium: never hung
marks.detail: The same Chromium binary, driven by Playwright with a fresh profile per launch, loaded these pages in several scripts tonight and always closed. It does not use --dump-dom, so it cannot tell a lock problem from an exit problem.

show.after:
$ node shot.js
start | 3 to go · 1 question | on stage: Check the anchor before replying
…
errors: []

marks.label: ask before the check: 4 ms
marks.detail: The baseline. Before the anchor check, jelly ask never started a browser.

show.after:
$ jelly ask plan "Which order?" … --at "#nope"
demo:plan v2: asked a1 "Which order?"; it shows on the page below #nope.
ms 4

marks.label: Check v1: right answer, after 8 s
marks.detail: The first anchor check waited for Chrome to exit, with an 8 s limit. It took all 8 s and still knew #nope matched nothing. The snapshot had arrived; only the exit was missing.

show.after:
$ jelly ask plan "Which order?" … --at "#nope"
demo:plan v2: asked a1 "Which order?"; #nope matches nothing on the page, so it shows at the top.
ms 8027

marks.label: 4 asks: 450, 8009, 8006, 8009 ms
marks.detail: Four asks in a row against one daemon. Every one got the right answer. One exited at once; three ran to the limit.

show.after:

asked a4 "Again 2?"; #nope matches nothing on the page, so it shows at the top.

asked a6 "Again 4?"; #nope matches nothing on the page, so it shows at the top.

marks.label: Fix: answer when the snapshot is in
marks.detail: The anchor check stops waiting for the process. It polls for the snapshot while the browser runs and drops the browser once it has one. jelly see was left as it is.

show.before:
let rendered = render(…).await;   // waits for Chrome to exit
for _ in 0..30 { if let Some(s) = snap() { return Ok(…) } … }
show.caption: anchor_place in src/server.rs

marks.detail: Seven asks in a row: 3745, 730, 725, 720, 725, 775 and 724 ms. All right. The first is unexplained.

marks.label: 2 Chrome processes still alive
marks.detail: Right after the seven asks. The check had already answered each time, so something of Chrome outlives the answer.

hypotheses.text: Chrome's first start on an empty profile is slow
hypotheses.why: My first guess, and what issue #6 says. It fits only the first two runs.
hypotheses.settle: Settled against: it keeps failing on a profile that has been warm for two hours.

hypotheses.text: Runs collide on the one shared profile and its lock
hypotheses.why: The lock files are there and runs alternate, but a locked-out Chrome would not render at all, and these do.
hypotheses.settle: Give every render its own profile folder and run jelly see fifty times. If the 20 s runs stop, it was the profile.

hypotheses.text: Chrome posts its snapshot, then does not exit, because the page keeps a WebSocket open
hypotheses.why: The first half is seen: right answers after 8 s, a snapshot with a timed-out screenshot, processes left over. The WebSocket as the reason is a guess, and it does not explain the runs that exit in 1 s.
hypotheses.settle: Serve the same view with the WebSocket stubbed out and render it twenty times with --dump-dom. Count how many exit on their own.
